newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia cocoa output seen 400,000 tonnes in 2000.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia cocoa output seen 400,000 tonnes in 2000.

text.p: Indonesia's cocoa output is expected to exceed 400,000 tonnes by the year 2000, according to a country report presented at a regional meeting on Tuesday.

"Indonesian cocoa production in the year 2000 will reach more than 400,000 tonnes ... and is projected to continue to increase in the following years," said the report presented at a meeting of Southeast Asian cocoa producers in Jakarta.
The country's 1997 production has been forecast by the Indonesian Cocoa Association at between 319,000 and 330,000 tonnes, up 10 percent from 1996.

The report said increases in production would be supported by rises in cocoa fat content and improvements in quality, through proper fermentation and other good manufacturing practices of pre- and post-harvest handling.

Indonesia's long-term plan is to unseat Ghana as the world's largest producer after the Ivory Coast. Ghana's official 1995/96 (October/September) production had been put at 400,000 tonnes, while London trader ED & F Man estimated it at 390,000 tonnes.
The report said the expansion of cocoa plantings would continue in the coming years, particularly by smallholders, based on their interpretation and expectations of market prices.
It said some problems that should be overcome urgently included low productivity and fat content, imperfections in the fermentation process and the pod borer pest.

"A national programme has been launched for the breeding and selection of higher yielding hybrids with higher fat content," the report said. It said trials on fermentation should be continued as part of efforts to improve the aroma and chocolate taste of Indonesian cocoa beans.

The report said about 42,000 hectares of cocoa plantings have been infested by the pod borer, adding that research and field trials were continuing in cooperation with foreign experts to curtail the pest.

Industry officials had said the Indonesia Cocoa Association was conducting field trials in the key growing region of South Sulawesi with the help of the American Cocoa Research Institute in a bid to defeat the pod borer, a larvae which penetrates the cocoa shell to feed on the kernel.
The report said that in the first nine months of last year, Indonesian exports of cocoa beans and products totalled 195,647 tonnes compared with 233,308 tonnes in calendar 1995.
